_comment: T154 — the source-change synthetic corpus (FR-053, SC-008). Each entry in `revisions` carries its FULL contract rather than a patch, so the loader can DIFF consecutive revisions and compare the computed diff against the declared `change_kinds`, `breaking` and `drifted_operations`. Nothing here is an oracle a reader typed: every declared field is recomputed by `__init__.py` from the two contracts either side of it, and a disagreement fails at load time. See README.md for why the non-breaking revisions are load-bearing rather than filler.
_comment_change_time: The source clock's change time IS the revision. There is no wall clock here and none is invented: SC-008 asks for detection `in the same automated check run as the commit that introduced them`, so the corpus controls its change time by binding exactly one check run to exactly one revision. The loader refuses a run that observes two revisions, because `the same run as the commit` is unfalsifiable once a run spans a range.

baseline_anchor._comment: The base revision's operation identifiers are asserted to be a subset of the reference application's published set, so this corpus describes drift on a target this repository actually has rather than on five invented names. Added operations at later revisions are new by construction and are exempt.

revisions.why: The base revision. It has no predecessor, so it can carry no diff and raises no signal. It exists so that every later revision is scored against a contract that was committed rather than assumed.

revisions.why: E13's first named mutation — rename a route. The loader verifies the rename is a rename and not a coincidence: the removed operation's parameters and returns must be identical to the added one's, or the declaration is refused. A structural differ that reports remove-plus-add is not wrong here, but it is a different signal and the corpus distinguishes them.

revisions.why: One revision carrying a breaking change AND a non-breaking one at once. A detector that stops at the first diff it finds, or that classifies a revision by its first change kind, gets this wrong in one direction or the other. `drifted_operations` names only the operation the BREAKING half touched, which is why the two kinds cannot be collapsed into a per-revision boolean and left there.
